key_insight: PIWF splits multiscale flow learning into a Fourier branch for global modes and a wavelet branch for localized sharp features, then fuses them with physics-informed training to better capture complex fluid dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical surrogate modeling strategy for engineering flows with shocks, fronts, wakes, and vortices when high-fidelity interior data are scarce.
method: Fourier branch models long-range coherent structures.
Wavelet branch captures compact, steep-gradient, and vortical features.
Residual MLP with channel attention fuses both branches under physics-informed losses.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on five benchmark problems—Burgers, shallow water, Kovasznay flow, Taylor–Green vortex, and 2D cylinder wake—showing improved resolution of gradients, interfaces, wakes, vorticity extrema, and spectra versus PINNs and PINNs-KAN.
watch_item: Performance may depend on careful balance between Fourier and wavelet components and the chosen physics-loss weighting, especially for highly stiff or noisy flows.
paper_title: Physics informed wavelet Fourier representation for multiscale fluid dynamics
